To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a generalized random walk model for biased cell motility is presented that accounts for the spatial or directional dependence in cell speed and turning behavior, and it is shown how the random walk parameters can be extracted from the observed cell migration data.

a generalized transport model for cell migration in the presence of spatial or directional dependence is presented and is applied to predict biased cell migration in gradients and along axes of anisotropies.

the random motility tensor for biased cell migration is a function of the underlying cell speed distribution, the cell turning behavior, and the anisotropy of the underlying environment, which is characterized by the stimulus gradient or anisotropy axis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a generalized transport model for cell migration that is applicable to a wide range of motility mechanisms.
developing a theoretical framework to describe biased cell migration in the presence of anisotropies and to relate it to the underlying motility mechanisms.
the development of mathematical models of the random motility of individual cells, and the application of these models to predict cell migration in anisotropic environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a generalized transport model for cell migration in a spatially varying environment is derived and applied to the specific case of biased cell migration.
cell motility and migration can be modeled in a general framework by a random walk model, and the resulting constitutive cell flux can be derived from this random walk model.
the generalized transport model is a powerful tool to describe biased cell migration in complex environments, which is a key feature of many biological systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a cell migration model based on a biased random walk is derived for a general case of anisotropic environments and applied to two special cases of cell migration: (1) biased cell migration along a gradient of an attractant and (2) biased cell movement along the axis of anisotropic environment.

we derived an analytical solution for the biased cell migration in the presence of anisotropies, which is the first time that the anisotropy of the environment was taken into account in the derivation.

we have derived a generalized transport model that can be used to predict cell flux in an anisotropy environment and that can be used in conjunction with experimental data to extract the underlying motility parameters of the random walk model.
The main takeaway from our work is that

biased cell migration in general is described by a random walk model with drift velocity and random motility tensor that are functions of the underlying motility parameters and the spatial and directional dependence of cell motility.
the random motility tensor, which is the key parameter for the cell flux equation, is determined by the underlying motility mechanisms of the cells.

the observed cell flux can be decomposed into the sum of a drift velocity and a diffusivity tensor that can be used to characterize cell migration in anisotropic environments, where the drift velocity is proportional to the bias in the underlying cell random walk and the diffusivity tensor is proportional to the variance of the underlying cell random walks.
